reasons: Behaviour depends on the browser, so manual checks are needed.

terms.meaning: A React function that lets a component read and react to state, such as a setting.
A browser check on the device or user setting, such as screen type or motion preference.
A browser technology for drawing 3D graphics.
A visitor setting that asks sites to limit animation.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File header and imports
sections.what: Marks the file as running in the browser and imports the two React tools it uses.
sections.why: The hooks read browser settings, which exist only in the visitor's browser.

sections.name: prefersReducedMotion
sections.title: Checks the reduced motion setting
sections.what: Asks the browser whether the visitor asked for less motion. Returns false when no browser is present.
sections.why: Likely reason: respects the visitor's accessibility choice.
sections.watch_out: On the server it returns false, so motion may show until the browser value is read.

sections.name: useReducedMotion
sections.title: Keeps the reduced motion setting live
sections.what: Gives a component a true or false value for reduced motion, and updates it if the visitor changes the setting while the page is open.
sections.why: Likely reason: the setting can change without a page reload.
sections.watch_out: The change listener is removed when the component is removed, so that cleanup must stay in place.

sections.name: useNoHover
sections.title: Detects touch-first devices
sections.what: Reports true on devices whose main input cannot hover, such as most phones and tablets, and keeps the value up to date.
sections.why: Likely reason: hover effects do not work on touch screens.
sections.watch_out: The value starts as false until the effect runs, so hover-only styling can briefly show on touch devices.

sections.name: hasWebGL
sections.title: Checks for 3D graphics support
sections.what: Tries to create a test canvas and reports whether WebGL 2 or WebGL is available. Returns false if there is no document or an error occurs.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets 3D features fall back when the browser cannot draw them.

summary: Four small hooks that report the visitor's motion setting, whether the device is touch-only, and whether 3D graphics are supported.
purpose: Lets the site reduce animation for some visitors and choose effects that the device can handle.
why: Likely reason: the names point to accessibility and device support. The code does not state this.
how: Each hook reads a browser setting, stores the result, and listens for changes to that setting.
inputs: Browser media queries and the document's canvas support.
outputs: True or false values for components to use.
risks: The starting values are defaults until the browser is read, so the first render can differ from the final one.
debug: In the browser's developer tools, check the reduced motion and hover settings, and whether a test canvas gets a WebGL context.
